concepts.label: Controlled execution
concepts.summary: A production work substrate that makes consequential execution authorized, observable, interruptible, reconstructable and testable.

concepts.label: Execution history
concepts.summary: A durable record of what happened during work so state, decisions and actions can be reconstructed later.

concepts.label: Protected data separation
concepts.summary: Separating orchestration visibility from broad access to protected business data and secrets.

concepts.label: Human-agent task equivalence
concepts.summary: Modeling work so the executor can move between an AI agent and a person without creating a separate exception process.

concepts.label: Replayable evaluation
concepts.summary: Using reconstructed historical execution state to evaluate models, prompts, policies and tools against past work.

concepts.label: Policy as code
concepts.summary: Representing authorization and policy decisions as explicit, reviewable rules rather than scattered application logic.

concepts.label: Observability
concepts.summary: Structured traces, metrics and logs that make distributed execution inspectable without becoming the source of business truth itself.

concepts.label: Durable execution
concepts.summary: Execution whose workflow progress survives process failure, waits and restarts because durable state exists outside any one Worker process.

concepts.label: Workflow Execution
concepts.summary: The durable Temporal unit representing one running workflow identity and its persisted progress over time.

concepts.label: Event History
concepts.summary: Temporal's append-only event record that represents Workflow Execution progress and supports state reconstruction.

concepts.label: Task Queue
concepts.summary: The Temporal dispatch boundary from which Worker Processes poll Workflow and Activity tasks for execution.

concepts.label: Worker Process
concepts.summary: A replaceable process that polls Temporal Task Queues and runs Workflow or Activity application code.

concepts.label: Activity Execution
concepts.summary: The Temporal boundary for side-effecting work that can interact with external systems and may be retried after failure.

concepts.label: Idempotency under retry
concepts.summary: Designing external effects so repeating a failed operation does not create unintended duplicate outcomes.

relations.rationale: Consequential work cannot be reconstructed or evaluated later without a durable history of execution.
Governed orchestration should not require broad access to protected data simply to observe or control work.
Production work needs a stable task model when execution moves between an agent and a human reviewer.
Explicit policy decisions make authorization boundaries reviewable and testable instead of implicit in application code.
Operators need structured telemetry to inspect execution health even when business evidence lives in a separate durable record.
Historical execution state becomes reusable evaluation material only when enough context can be reconstructed reliably.
Durability solves continuity of execution while controlled execution adds governance, authority, evidence and intervention around that work.
Temporal realizes durable work as a persisted Workflow Execution rather than tying workflow state to one running process.
Persisted Event History is the record from which Workflow Execution progress can be reconstructed after Worker failure.
Worker Processes execute application code for the durable Workflow Execution while remaining replaceable executors.
Workers receive executable Workflow and Activity tasks by polling the configured Temporal Task Queue.
Workers execute Activity code as one of the main boundaries where Temporal applications interact with external systems.
Activity retries can repeat external work, so safe side effects require idempotent or otherwise duplicate-safe design.
Temporal Event History is a concrete implementation-level example of the broader execution-history concept used in production architecture.
